references.text: John 10:29 emphasizes that no one can snatch away those given to God, which directly mirrors Psalm 31:24 where David prays that those who hope in the Lord should be strong and their hearts strengthened, implying God's protection against enemies.

Both texts highlight God's presence as a source of security in dangerous situations; while John 10:29 speaks of no one being able to snatch away from the Father's hand, Psalm 23:4 promises that one will fear no evil when God is with them.
John 10:29 confirms that no one can snatch away from the Father, which corresponds with Isaiah 43:13 where it is stated that no one can deliver from God's hand and that He acts without opposition.

John 10:29 promises that no one can snatch away those given to God, which is a direct parallel to Isaiah 49:25-26 where the prophet declares that even the strongest warriors cannot snatch away God's captives, for the Lord will punish those who take them.

In John 17:11-12, Jesus prays that the disciples be kept in the Father's name and that none of them were lost except the son of perdition, which reflects the theme in John 10:29 that no one can snatch away from the Father's hand.

John 6:39-40 expresses God's will that He should lose none of those He has given to Jesus, which serves as a direct theological foundation for the claim in John 10:29 that no one can snatch away from the Father's hand.
